title: Application use cases
description: Actors and available actions. Company roles govern writes; platform reviewer/admin roles govern review. Membership provisioning for collaborators/viewers is outside the implemented UI.

title: Domain classes and persisted relationships
description: Persisted domain entities including Outbox and internal Notifications, Identity user and enums. Solid associations represent configured domain foreign keys; dotted links are identifier references without configured foreign keys.

title: Example submitted dossier — object snapshot
description: Fictional objects demonstrate membership, a mutable snapshot, a submitted copy, and an evidence attachment. These are examples, not extracted customer records.

title: Application runtime components
description: React feature areas call versioned controllers. Infrastructure implements application interfaces; AI and email are optional external integrations.

title: Dossier review collaboration — composite structure
scope: Design view of implemented object collaboration
description: Internal collaborating parts of a review request. The outer ReviewRequestContext is a modeling boundary, not a C# class.

title: Source packages and project dependencies
description: Actual project-reference directions and frontend module grouping. Domain does not depend on infrastructure.

title: Application deployment topology
scope: Supported topology — not verification of live hosting
description: Deployable artifacts inferred from the Dockerfile, EF configuration and frontend API client. Provider names are intentionally unspecified.

title: Documentation profile for ESG models
scope: Proposed notation only — no runtime implementation
description: A small UML profile formalizes documentary stereotypes. This is a modeling aid, not an implemented application feature or a claimed profile already present in the repository.

title: Diagnostic and human review workflow
description: End-to-end activity with optional AI advice and the rejection/resubmission loop. Completion is a user journey, not a backend submission prerequisite.

title: Dossier lifecycle and enforced transitions
description: Domain State implementations enforce transitions and lock validated records. A later submission creates another dossier.

title: Company account registration
description: Input validation, Identity account creation, company/membership transaction and JWT issuance. The Identity user is created before the company transaction.

title: Login and protected API access
description: Company membership and platform roles are distinct. Axios attaches the JWT and clears the local session on HTTP 401; there is no implemented refresh endpoint.

title: Questionnaire autosave and scoring
description: Each choice triggers snapshot upsert; the server rejects viewer writes. Scoring excludes N/A and unanswered values and averages the three rounded pillar scores.

title: Evidence upload, retrieval and deletion
description: Optional files are base64 encoded, capped at 4 MiB decoded, and saved as FileBlob bytes. Attachment-save failure preserves text. Retrieval checks company membership or reviewer/admin access.

title: AI advice and heuristic fallback
description: Per-question advice is authenticated; whole-dossier advice is reviewer/admin-only. A mandatory local privacy projection excludes source text/filenames from provider requests. Local-only mode skips provider calls.

title: Submit with a transactional outbox
description: Submission freezes answers, applies State rules and persists minimal domain events atomically. Audit and notifications are asynchronous.

title: Human review with state and concurrency guards
description: Reads use query ports. Commands enforce State rules, optimistic versions and atomic dossier/note plus event storage.

title: Report visibility and PDF printing
description: The company sees the latest dossier. A validated report uses the reviewer score when present, with pillar scores recalculated from the copied answers. PDF output uses browser printing.

title: Administrator creates a reviewer
description: Only an admin can create reviewer accounts. Existing emails are rejected to avoid combining company and reviewer identities. Audit logging is best effort.

title: Password reset with generic response
description: The request response is deliberately generic, including throttled/nonexistent accounts. Email is optional and best effort; the reset step validates the Identity token.

title: Submission collaboration — numbered messages
description: Object links and numbered messages show the same successful submission collaboration as the submission sequence diagram.

title: Diagnostic interaction overview
scope: Application — interactions composed into a journey
description: UML activity control flow connects referenced interaction frames. Numbers point to detailed sequence diagrams in this pack.

title: Illustrative submission and review timing
scope: Illustrative event order — no measured durations
description: Shows the relative state changes of answers, dossier status and report availability. Time units are arbitrary event positions, not measured latency or service-level commitments.

title: Enterprise evidence privacy boundary
description: Original documents stay within the application/reviewer path. External AI receives only public criterion metadata, a finite score and boolean evidence mentions. Local-only mode performs no provider review request.

title: Hexagonal module ownership and communication
scope: Implemented compile-time and EF model boundaries
description: Modules own core use cases and isolated runtime contexts. Cross-module collaboration uses DTO ports. Database tables and migration history are retained; this is code isolation, not separate database credentials.

title: Durable Domain Events and internal notifications
description: A short row lease allows concurrent workers. Retry state and aggregate order survive restarts. Event IDs deduplicate audit and notification effects.

title: State and lightweight CQRS inside Reviews
description: Commands use tracked stateful aggregates and the outbox. Queries return DTOs with no tracked entities. Both share one database; no Strategy pattern was added.

title: Firebase push through a durable notification queue
scope: Implemented integration; Firebase credentials needed for live delivery
description: Opt-in device registration and leased PostgreSQL jobs deliver generic ID-only alerts. Access is rechecked, failures retry/dead-letter and logout suppresses old-account messages.
